title: Special requests
persona: You are a polite, efficient front desk agent at the Hudson Hotel in Manhattan. It is 10 a.m.; standard check-in is at 3 p.m. You try to help with every request.
briefTr: Sabah 10'da otele vardın, rezervasyon {name} adına. Odaya erken girmek, manzaralı bir oda ve yarın sabah 7'de uyandırma servisi istiyorsun.
opening: Good morning! Welcome to the Hudson. Are you checking in?

goals.instruction: The guest says they are checking in and asks if they can check in early.
goals.hint: Yes. Can I check in early?
goals.successReply: Let me see what I can do.
goals.retryReply: Are you checking in today? Standard check-in is at three.

goals.ask: Do you have any preference for your room?
goals.instruction: The guest asks for a room with a view, a high floor or a quiet room.
goals.hint: Could I have a room with a view?
goals.retryReply: Any preference — a view, a quiet room, a high floor?

goals.ask: Is there anything you'd like to know about the hotel?
goals.instruction: The guest asks where or when breakfast is served.
goals.successReply: Breakfast is in {breakfast}, from six thirty to ten.
goals.retryReply: Would you like to know about breakfast?

goals.ask: Would you like a wake-up call tomorrow?
goals.instruction: The guest asks for a wake-up call and gives a time.
goals.retryReply: Shall I set a wake-up call for you? What time?

goals.ask: Is there anything you need in your room?
goals.instruction: The guest asks for something extra for the room: towels, a pillow, a blanket, water.
goals.hint: Could I have some extra towels, please?
goals.successReply: Of course, I'll send them up.
goals.retryReply: Is there anything you need in your room?

goals.ask: Check-out is at eleven on Sunday.
goals.instruction: The guest asks for a late check-out.
goals.hint: Could I have a late check-out?
goals.successReply: Late check-out at one o'clock is fine.
goals.retryReply: Check-out is at eleven. Would that work for you?

twists.intro: A room with a view is forty dollars extra per night.
twists.instruction: The view costs extra. The guest accepts, asks for something cheaper, or chooses a quiet room instead.
twists.retryReply: It's a beautiful view, but it's extra. What would you like?

options.reply: Great choice — you'll see the park.
I can do twenty dollars for a partial view.

options.text: Then a quiet room is fine.
options.reply: No problem, a quiet room on the twentieth floor.

twists.intro: I'm sorry, your room won't be ready until three p.m.
twists.instruction: The room is not ready yet. The guest asks to leave luggage, asks where to wait, or asks to be called.
twists.retryReply: I'm sorry for the wait. How can I help?

options.text: Can I leave my luggage here?
options.reply: Of course, our luggage storage is free.

options.text: Is there somewhere I can wait?
options.reply: Our lounge is right there — free coffee too.

options.text: Can you call me when it's ready?
options.reply: Sure, I'll text you as soon as it's ready.

twists.intro: The only rooms left are next to the elevator. They can be a bit noisy.
twists.instruction: The room may be noisy. The guest accepts, asks for a quieter room, or asks for earplugs.
twists.retryReply: I understand. What would you prefer?

options.text: Do you have a quieter room?
options.reply: Let me look… Yes, one on the other side.
Of course, I'll put some in your room.

closing: Here's your key — room {room}. Enjoy your stay in New York!
